name: Macular Amyloidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Macular Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, pruritic, hyperpigmented macules with a rippled or reticulated pattern primarily on the upper back and extensor surfaces
Skin biopsy showing amyloid deposits in the papillary dermis confirmed by Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Exclusion of systemic amyloidosis and other causes of cutaneous hyperpigmentation
Dermoscopy revealing characteristic brownish pigmentation with a central hub and radial streaks

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical presentation plus histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits in skin biopsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical features supported by histopathology; systemic involvement is absent.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent pruritic hyperpigmented macules with rippled pattern
searchTerms: itchy dark spots with rippled pattern

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposits localized to papillary dermis
searchTerms: amyloid deposits in upper skin layer
protein buildup in skin papillary dermis

common.symptomName: Chronic pruritus localized to affected skin areas
searchTerms: chronic itchy skin in affected areas

common.symptomName: Symmetrical distribution of hyperpigmented macules on upper back and arms
searchTerms: symmetrical dark spots on upper back and arms
balanced skin spots on back and arms

common.symptomName: Mild skin thickening or lichenification in chronic cases

occasional.symptomName: Mild scaling or xerosis over affected areas
Occasional involvement of chest and abdomen

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection due to excoriation

searchTerms: small swollen lymph nodes in area

laboratory: Skin biopsy with Congo red staining showing amyloid deposits
Negative systemic amyloidosis workup (serum and urine protein electrophoresis)
imaging: Dermoscopy showing central hub with radial pigmentation streaks
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible familial predisposition in some cases
other: Absence of systemic involvement differentiates from systemic amyloidosis

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology shows amyloid deposits in papillary dermis but with different clinical morphology
History of preceding inflammatory skin condition
Absence of amyloid deposits on biopsy
Systemic symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, organ involvement
Positive serum or urine markers for systemic amyloid

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or fatigue
Signs suggestive of systemic amyloidosis (e.g., nephrotic syndrome, cardiomyopathy)
references: Wang SQ, et al. Macular Amyloidosis: Clinical Features and Pathogenesis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019;80(3):789-795.
